long_biography.plain_text:
Google cofounder Larry Page initially wanted to map the web's links, without planning a search engine. At twenty-three, he woke from a dream about downloading the web and worked through the idea on paper. His adviser, Terry Winograd, encouraged the research; a better way to rank web pages emerged from it.

Page also helped design Google's unusual shareholder structure. At its flotation, shares carrying different voting rights preserved the founders' influence. He and Brin defended that arrangement as protection for projects requiring years of investment, citing Android's lengthy development. They later proposed non-voting shares so employee share awards and acquisitions would not steadily erode that control.
long_biography.html:
Google cofounder Larry Page initially wanted to map the web's links, without planning a search engine. At twenty-three, he woke from a dream about downloading the web and worked through the idea on paper. His adviser, Terry Winograd, encouraged the research; a better way to rank web pages emerged from it.

Page also helped design Google's unusual shareholder structure. At its flotation, shares carrying different voting rights preserved the founders' influence. He and Brin defended that arrangement as protection for projects requiring years of investment, citing Android's lengthy development. They later proposed non-voting shares so employee share awards and acquisitions would not steadily erode that control.
